title: LDL-lowering medications: how to get a 20%, 50%, or 80% reduction
summary: Compare statin doses, non-statin medications, and combinations by how much they lower LDL.
body_markdown:
Modern medicines are miracles that can lower LDL cholesterol by up to 85%. Which exact set of medications are right for you is a conversation between you and your doctor, and partly depends on your starting point. An LDL cholesterol of 160 mg/dL will almost certainly need medications to reach <100 mg/dL, whereas an LDL of 110 mg/dL might be in the range for lifestyle.


This guide walks through all of the interventions that lower your LDL: diet, statins, Zetia, PCSK9 inhibitors, and more.


We’ll work backward from the reduction you need, using a cheat sheet built from our intervention evidence database. Then we’ll answer how much each medication lowers LDL, compare common choices, and show what combining them could achieve. Our[ApoB medication guide](https://www.empirical.health/blog/apob-lowering-medications/) covers the related particle measurement; the numbers here refer specifically to LDL cholesterol.


## How much do you need to lower LDL cholesterol?


The[2026 AHA/ACC guidelines](https://professional.heart.org/en/science-news/2026-guideline-on-the-management-of-dyslipidemia) set LDL targets below 100, 70, or 55 mg/dL, depending on cardiovascular risk and medical history. For the target you and your clinician choose:


**Required reduction = (current LDL − target LDL) ÷ current LDL × 100.**


Starting LDL (mg/dL) Target LDL (mg/dL) Example medications Reduction


125 100 Add ezetimibe 10 mg to existing therapy 20%


160 100 Atorvastatin 20 mg or simvastatin 40 mg About 38%


140 70 Rosuvastatin 20 mg or atorvastatin 80 mg 50%


180 70 Rosuvastatin 20 mg + ezetimibe 10 mg About 61%


275 55 Rosuvastatin 20 mg + ezetimibe 10 mg + evolocumab 80%


The percentages show the change from starting to target LDL; the medications can provide roughly that reduction or more. Only the first row starts from treated LDL. Responses vary; combination estimates use the calculation below.


## Which medications lower LDL cholesterol the most?


The cheat sheet compares medication doses, dietary changes, and two calculated combinations:


*Circles: changes from baseline. Diamonds: differences versus the study comparator. Squares: calculated combinations. Whiskers: 95% confidence intervals, not individual response ranges. Populations, background therapy, and follow-up differ.[Data and sources](https://www.empirical.health/data/ldl-medications/intervention-effects.csv) .*


## How much does each statin lower LDL?


Statins help the liver make less cholesterol and clear more LDL from blood. All seven have generic versions; prices depend on the pharmacy, dose, and insurance.


- **Rosuvastatin (Crestor)** lowers LDL about 46% at 10 mg/day, 52% at 20 mg, and 55% at 40 mg. Muscle-injury risk rises at 40 mg; severe kidney impairment limits dosing to 10 mg/day in patients not on hemodialysis.[Prescribing information](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/021366s040s041lbl.pdf) .
- **Atorvastatin (Lipitor)** lowers LDL about 37% at 10 mg/day, 43% at 20 mg, 48% at 40 mg, and 51% at 80 mg, similar to rosuvastatin 20 mg’s 52%. It needs no kidney-based dose adjustment, though certain antibiotics and antivirals can raise drug levels and muscle-injury risk.[Prescribing information](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=a60cc18b-0631-4cf0-b021-9f52224ece65) .
- **Simvastatin (Zocor)** lowers LDL about 28% at 10 mg/day, 35% at 20 mg, and 39% at 40 mg. Walmart lists those strengths at[$9 for 30 tablets](https://i5.walmartimages.com/dfw/4ff9c6c9-119c/k2-_c3e2f451-7a63-414e-aac2-e3defc13ef60.v1.pdf) , with state and program restrictions. Avoid starting or increasing to 80 mg because of muscle-injury risk; interactions can also limit dosing.[Prescribing information](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/lookup.cfm?setid=ca760e79-5d8c-4b36-9899-0d37e8e1f24e) .
- **Pravastatin (Pravachol)** lowers LDL about 20% at 10 mg/day, 24% at 20 mg, and 30% at 40 mg. It has fewer drug interactions, though muscle symptoms remain possible. See the[ACC’s statin comparison tool](https://tools.acc.org/StatinIntolerance/index.html) .
- **Lovastatin** lowered LDL about 24% at 20 mg once daily, 30% at 40 mg once daily, and 40% at 40 mg twice daily in EXCEL. Grapefruit and certain antibiotics or antifungals can increase lovastatin levels and muscle-injury risk.[Trial results and prescribing information](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/lookup.cfm?setid=8d8199ca-df39-4eb8-a905-dee3ab7e2973) .
- **Pitavastatin (Livalo, Zypitamag)** lowers LDL about 31% at 1 mg/day, 39% at 2 mg, and 44% at 4 mg. Muscle symptoms remain possible; moderate or severe kidney impairment limits dosing to 2 mg/day.[Prescribing information](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=7fbfcc0c-9251-456d-a525-e62cfd8abd4b) .
- **Fluvastatin (Lescol)** lowers LDL about 22% at 20 mg/day, 25% at 40 mg/day, and 36% at 40 mg twice daily. Fluconazole raises its levels and requires a dose limit for the capsules.[Trial results and prescribing information](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/lookup.cfm?setid=e38126a5-9d6a-422f-812c-a01610108162) .


The first four report six-week averages from[STELLAR](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0002-9149(03)00530-7) . The others use separate studies: EXCEL weeks 12–48, pitavastatin at 12 weeks in older adults, and fluvastatin medians at 24 weeks. Individual responses vary. Our[statin guide](https://www.empirical.health/blog/statins-compared/) covers other differences.


## How much do non-statin medications lower LDL?


- **Ezetimibe (Zetia)** blocks intestinal cholesterol absorption. At 10 mg/day, it lowered LDL an additional[21% on a statin](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0002-9149(02)02774-1) , or[17% versus placebo when used alone](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0002-9149(02)02798-4) . Adding it to a statin also reduced cardiovascular events after acute coronary syndrome in[IMPROVE-IT](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1410489) .
- **Increase the statin dose or add ezetimibe?** Doubling atorvastatin from 10 to 20 mg increased LDL lowering from 37% to 43% in STELLAR. In[RACING](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0140673622009163) , rosuvastatin 10 mg + ezetimibe 10 mg performed similarly to rosuvastatin 20 mg for cardiovascular events, with more patients reaching LDL below 70 and fewer reducing or stopping treatment because of side effects.
- **Bempedoic acid (Nexletol)** lowered LDL an additional[18% versus placebo on existing therapy](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1803917) at 180 mg/day, and reduced cardiovascular events in[statin-intolerant patients](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2215024) . Combined with ezetimibe as Nexlizet, it lowered LDL 38% versus placebo. Gout and tendon injury are important risks.[Prescribing information](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=3fa2108c-0300-47b8-9d34-f762af7c93c6) .
- **PCSK9 inhibitors** can lower LDL roughly another 50–60% on existing therapy. See thecomparison below for medications, dosing, and cash prices.


## PCSK9 antibodies can cost $225–$239/month cash and lower LDL about 60%


Evolocumab (Repatha) and alirocumab (Praluent) block PCSK9, preserving liver LDL receptors that clear cholesterol from blood. US cash programs advertise[Praluent at $225 for two pens](https://trumprx.gov/p/praluent) and[Repatha at $239/month](https://www-ext.amgen.com/newsroom/press-releases/2025/10/amgen-makes-repatha-available-through-amgennow-a-directtopatient-program-in-the-us) . September 2026 cash prices; eligibility requirements apply and insurance costs differ.


*The oral PCSK9 inhibitor enlicitide (yellow) binds PCSK9 (teal), helping preserve LDL receptors (green) that clear cholesterol from blood. Read more about[how this peptide works](https://www.empirical.health/blog/macrocyclic-peptides/) . Image: Merck & Co., Inc., via[The Scientist](https://www.the-scientist.com/engineered-enzymes-streamline-synthesis-of-an-oral-cholesterol-drug-74558) .*


Medication LDL reduction Treatment context


Repatha 59% versus placebo at 48 weeks On statins; 140 mg every two weeks or 420 mg monthly.[FOURIER](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1615664)


Praluent 47.2% from baseline Alone; 75 mg every two weeks, increased to 150 mg per protocol.[ODYSSEY MONO](https://doi.org/10.2217/fca.14.82)


Praluent 62-percentage-point advantage over placebo at 24 weeks On statins; 150 mg every two weeks.[ODYSSEY LONG TERM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1501031)


Inclisiran (Leqvio) 49.9–52.3% versus placebo at day 510 On existing therapy; reduces PCSK9 production. Given initially, at three months, then every six months.[ORION](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1912387) ;[label](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/214012s016lbl.pdf)


Lerodalcibep (Lerochol) About 50–59% versus placebo On existing therapy; 300 mg monthly injection.[FDA](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-trials-snapshots/drug-trials-snapshots-lerochol)


Enlicitide (Lipfendra) 56% versus placebo in CORALreef Lipids; 59% in heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, at 24 weeks On existing therapy; 20 mg daily pill.[Label](https://www.dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=100ec543-fbd0-44fc-b740-db9cdff39145)


Trial populations and regimens differ; similar LDL reductions don’t establish equal cardiovascular benefits. Lerochol and Lipfendra aren’t in the chart yet. Our[Lipfendra guide](https://www.empirical.health/blog/oral-pcsk9-inhibitor-lipfendra/) explains its fasting requirements.


## Other LDL-lowering medications


Bile-acid sequestrants (colesevelam, cholestyramine, and colestipol) lower LDL roughly[10–27%](https://www.acc.org/Latest-in-Cardiology/Articles/2026/09/01/01/Feature-Getting-to-Goals) . Colesevelam lowered it[15% at about 3.8 g/day](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/lookup.cfm?setid=b48a7426-b513-4790-99a4-4f07d83318d7) . Constipation, medication interactions, and increased triglycerides can limit their use.


Two specialist drugs treat homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH), a rare inherited condition:


Medication LDL result in HoFH Main considerations


Evinacumab (Evkeeza) 49% versus placebo at 24 weeks on background therapy Monthly infusion; works despite severely impaired LDL-receptor function.[FDA label](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/761181s002lbl.pdf)


Lomitapide (Juxtapid) 40% mean reduction from baseline at 26 weeks, adult intent-to-treat analysis Requires liver monitoring, dietary restrictions, and interaction review.[Label](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=61a0be9d-ee58-43e0-b5cb-141011835081)


Niacin lowers LDL, but adding it to intensive statin therapy didn’t reduce cardiovascular events in[AIM-HIGH](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1107579) . Fibrates mainly treat high triglycerides:[fenofibrate lowered LDL 20.6%](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=5c579378-e00e-4802-b9d3-c062cf8bd9f4) in elevated-LDL trials, while[gemfibrozil can raise LDL](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/lookup.cfm?setid=85c59fe5-5cac-4cf5-915b-2aba2a787765) when triglycerides are very high.


## How much can rosuvastatin + ezetimibe + a PCSK9 inhibitor lower LDL?


Each added medication lowers the LDL remaining. For rosuvastatin 20 mg, ezetimibe 10 mg, and evolocumab, use decimals (52% = 0.52):


**Combined reduction = 1 − (1 − statin effect) × (1 − ezetimibe effect) × (1 − PCSK9 effect).**


Starting at 160 mg/dL, this estimates LDL of 77 with rosuvastatin, 60 after adding ezetimibe, and 25 after adding evolocumab: reductions of 52%, 62%, and 85%.


*Calculated using 52%, 21.4%, and 59% effects from separate trials, assuming each transfers to the combined regimen. These are illustrative estimates, not observed combination-trial results, individual forecasts, or recommended targets.*


## Statins vs PCSK9 inhibitors


High-intensity statins lower LDL roughly in half. In[FOURIER](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1615664) , evolocumab lowered LDL another 59% versus placebo on statins. The choice depends on dosing, coverage, side effects, and cardiovascular benefits. See our[comparison](https://www.empirical.health/blog/statins-vs-pcsk9-inhibitors/) and[insurance guide](https://www.empirical.health/blog/pcsk9-inhibitor-insurance-coverage/) .


## What if you can’t tolerate a statin?


Your clinician can review symptoms and interactions, then try a different statin or lower dose. Alternatives include ezetimibe, bempedoic acid, PCSK9 treatments, and bile-acid sequestrants.


## When should you recheck LDL after changing medication?


The[2026 guideline](https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/CIR.0000000000001423) recommends a lipid profile 4–12 weeks after starting or intensifying treatment. Use the result to calculate how much further LDL needs to fall.
